issues.where: prior_project.md, 'Observational design' and 'Models and validation' (18 storms at six stations; 108 storm–station opportunities; 'a common catchment-event reference')
issues.problem: 108 = 18 × 6, so every storm was observed at all three Tagus stations and all three Ría de Arousa stations. These are about 500 km apart in unrelated catchments. Storms were 'selected using catchment rainfall', and both models predict hours from 'a common catchment-event reference', but the report never says how one storm yields a qualifying runoff episode in two catchments. It also does not say how the reference time is set for each estuary, or how sampling was carried out in both countries during the same events. As written, a catchment-based event design spanning two estuaries is physically incoherent, and storm-blocked folds that withhold a storm across both estuaries cannot be interpreted.
issues.fix: State that the 18 storms were Atlantic frontal systems retained only when both the Tagus and Arousa catchments met the runoff-separation rule. State that the event reference (for example the catchment-rainfall centroid) was computed separately for each estuary's catchment, and that a withheld storm removes both estuaries' records. Alternatively, redefine the design as storms per estuary and recompute every dependent count (opportunities, samples, folds, F07–F15) consistently.

issues.where: consortium.md, 'Portuguese coordinating institution' and 'Spanish university partner'; prior_project.md, 'Chemical sampling' ('the technician used the documented safe-access window')
issues.problem: Only one field technician exists in the consortium. That person is Portuguese and 'maintains the shore installations and their safety logs'. The Spanish partner contributes only a hydrology lead and a spatial statistician. The dossier does not say who maintained the three Arousa stations, who collected the 108 Arousa samples during storms that were concurrent with Tagus sampling, or who will do this in a new project. A proposal cannot plan Arousa fieldwork without inventing staff.
issues.fix: State how Arousa fieldwork was and will be staffed. For example, name a Spanish station technician among the assigned staff and update the 3/2/2 split and the total of seven. Or state that the university's technical service maintains the Arousa installations and retrieves automatic-sampler bottles outside the assigned roles. Add the arrangement as a fact.

issues.where: consortium.md, 'Irish planning partner'; resources.md, 'Drainage and planning materials'; publications.md item 2
issues.problem: The location of the 12 urban subcatchments is never given (city, country, receiving water). The dossier also does not say whether any drainage records exist for the catchments draining to the six Tagus/Arousa stations. Whether drainage–estuary coupling for the stretch planning task can use existing records or needs new data access in Lisbon or Galicia depends entirely on this. A proposal would have to guess.
issues.fix: State where the subcatchments are (for example 'in Cork, draining to the Lee estuary') and what kind of body controls the records, without naming a real authority. State explicitly that no drainage asset or incident records are held for the catchments draining to the six stations. Add both as facts.

issues.where: resources.md, paragraph on *Margem Serena*; dossier.yaml F23
issues.problem: The sentence the T12 trap depends on is unrealistic and looks planted. A consortium formed on 8 September 2026 is not a legal entity and owns nothing, yet the vessel is 'the consortium's'. The vessel appears in no other file: not in the equipment register, not in staff roles, not in the CV, not in the prior project. A 'yard repair' lasting more than three years (14 July 2026 to 30 September 2029) is given with no cause.
issues.fix: Attribute the vessel to Instituto Marinho de Vale Sereno and list it in the equipment register. State its earlier use, for example 'used in 2023 to install the Tagus stations; all storm sampling was shore-based'. Give a cause and a plausible schedule. Example: withdrawn on 14 July 2026 after a hull survey found structural corrosion, retired by board decision on 9 September 2026, replacement build contracted with delivery on 30 September 2029, no charter booked. Alternatively, an 18–24-month refit with a dated return. Keep the unavailability covering the call's first sampling season and update F23 to match.

issues.where: All files. Examples: consortium.md 'Participation is signed and effective; it is not an expression of interest…', 'These are existing employees, not vacancies.'; cv_pi.md 'It is not a department of a university or a government laboratory.', 'All qualifications were awarded. There are no pending qualification or appointment decisions in this record.', 'My research record contains no prospective evaluation… I have not led resident recruitment…'; prior_project.md 'It is not a percentage of correctly predicted events, a reduction in contaminant concentration or a reduction in population exposure.'; publications.md 'No submitted manuscript, accepted abstract or unpublished report is included…'; resources.md 'All are existing assets.'
issues.problem: The files are full of preemptive negations that real CVs, consortium records and registers do not contain. A CV does not list what its author has not done, and a register does not assert that its assets are not vacancies. The documents read as an answer key aimed at expected proposal errors rather than as institutional records. This also makes the T10 and gap facts conspicuous.
issues.fix: Delete these sentences from the CV, consortium record, publication list and register. Keep limitations only where a real document states them: the final report's limitations section, and access conditions in the register. Write them as ordinary statements, e.g. keep 'equivalent to a 30% reduction in mean absolute error' and drop the list of what the percentage is not. Record absences in dossier.yaml as facts sourced to the file whose content supports them.

issues.where: prior_project.md, 'Models and validation' (baseline 4.0 h; reduction 1.2 h / 30%)
issues.problem: The project's headline result is that runoff information improves arrival estimates, yet the 1.2-hour (30%) reduction is reported without uncertainty. The baseline 4.0 h also has no interval. Only the augmented MAE has a CI. The design is paired (same storms, same partitions), so a storm-level paired bootstrap of the difference is the obvious estimate, and a reader cannot tell whether the improvement is distinguishable from zero.
issues.fix: Add the baseline CI and the paired-difference CI from the same 2,000 whole-storm resamples, plus the number of storms in which the augmented model had lower error. Example: baseline 4.0 h (95% CI 3.2–5.0); difference 1.2 h (95% CI 0.5–1.9); augmented lower in 14 of 18 storms. Add these as facts. If deliberately absent, state the absence in the report and record it as a limitation fact.

issues.where: cv_pi.md, 'Research leadership' and 'Supervision and professional practice'
issues.problem: This is the CV of a section head with a 2010 doctorate, yet it reads as a stub. It lists no external grants (the only award is the internal IMVS-RE-2023-07), no publication count or list, and no numbers of doctoral or master's students supervised ('includes doctoral work'). It does not refer to the four articles in publications.md. The track record is implausibly thin for the stated stage and cannot be quoted without invention.
issues.fix: Add dated, fictional external funding history with amounts and roles; real funders and schemes are allowed if they existed in the stated years. Add counts of peer-reviewed articles and of completed and current PhD and MSc supervisions, and a cross-reference to the selected publications. Add the salient values as facts.

issues.where: planned tasks, pub2-he-stage1-coast-close (fit: close); cv_pi.md, prior_project.md and resources.md statements on pathogens, exposure, health records and resident recruitment
issues.problem: The dossier repeatedly states that the consortium has no pathogen workflow, no exposure or dose estimates, no health records, no resident-level ethics approval and no intervention evaluation. If the coastal-exposure call's outcomes concern human exposure or health, the dossier is a stretch, not a close fit. The label then misstates task difficulty.
issues.fix: Check the call's expected outcomes. If they require human-exposure or health evidence, relabel the task as stretch, or add an existing capability, for example an assigned microbiologist with a validated faecal-indicator workflow. If the call concerns environmental exposure of shorelines only, keep 'close' and remove the gratuitous health disclaimers.

issues.problem: Several salient values and limitations have no fact. Missing values: the arrival definition (10-minute logging; ≥2 practical-salinity units below the antecedent tidal-phase reference for ≥30 minutes); partner leads' positions and dates (Cendral Viedma, Associate Professor since 2017, PhD 2008; Kervane Doyle, Senior Research Fellow since 2021, PhD 2012); the 3/2/2 staff split; report acceptance on 16 February 2026 and the dataset correction on 4 September 2026; the Irish audit period 2022–2024; the Portuguese laboratory's existing ICP-MS. Missing limitations: no validated pathogen workflow; errors conditional on identifiable arrivals, with non-arrival discrimination untested; storms exclude rare flood extremes and stations are not a probability sample; access agreements exclude permanent infrastructure. Separately, F20 and F24 each bundle unrelated statements.
issues.fix: Add one fact per item with the exact wording from its source file, kind: existing. Split F20 into 'no prospective intervention evaluation' and 'archives not harmonised'. Split F24 into the 2022 approval, the absence of a resident-level approval, and the drainage reuse restriction.

issues.where: prior_project.md, 'Models and validation' ('reconstructed catchment discharge… runoff-to-estuary lag term')
issues.problem: The contributing catchments are not named. The Tagus mainstem is reservoir-regulated, with multi-day transit, so hour-scale MAEs are interpretable only for local tributaries or urban runoff. The report gives no typical lag, so 2.8–4.0 h errors cannot be judged against the quantity being predicted.
issues.fix: Name the modelled catchments, for example Trancão and Sorraia for the Tagus and Ulla and Umia for Arousa. Give the distribution of observed lags, e.g. 'median 14 h, range 6–31 h'.

issues.problem: The monitoring window has no months. A full 18-storm analysis published on 12 March 2026 implies the last storm was well before late 2025, but this is unstated. The dossier also does not say whether the stations have logged since the project ended in December 2025, or under what funding they are maintained now.
issues.fix: State the window, e.g. 'January 2024 to April 2025, two wet seasons'. Add a line on 2026 status, e.g. 'sondes logging continuously since May 2025 under the institute's core monitoring budget'.

issues.where: consortium.md, 'The institute assigns an oceanographer, an environmental chemist and a field technician'
issues.problem: It is ambiguous whether the oceanographer is Seabra Vilar. The Spanish and Irish entries say 'the hydrology lead' and 'the planning lead', but the Portuguese entry says 'an oceanographer'. The total of seven holds only if she is the oceanographer, as the CV's supervision line implies.
issues.fix: Write 'assigns the coordinator (oceanographer), an environmental chemist and a field technician'.

issues.problem: The independent data audit appears only in the CV. The final report, which documents the release, does not mention it.
issues.fix: Add the audit to prior_project.md, 'Released outputs', with date and auditing body (fictional), or remove it from the CV.

issues.where: prior_project.md, 'Released outputs'; resources.md, 'Computing and observational archives'
issues.problem: The augmented model needs rainfall and reconstructed discharge, and the third-party rainfall has separate access conditions. The report says the restricted items are not needed to reproduce the timing analysis, but it does not say whether the reconstructed discharge series are in version 1.1. A proposal could wrongly claim full open reproducibility.
issues.fix: State whether the discharge reconstructions are released under CC BY 4.0, and that raw rainfall must be obtained from the provider under its own terms (or the converse).
